totals.rows_scoped: contract.invariants, contract.not_exposed, instructions and best_practices across the six assigned build-layer skills (build-adapter-pair, build-ceremony, build-definition-of-done, build-entry-conformance, build-evidence-record, build-interface-versioning). definition_of_done, adapters and composes_with were off limits per instruction and not touched in any of the six.

method: Same method as sourcing-01/02b/02c: for each origin=proposed row, ran python3 tools/kb.py show plus grep -i over kb/facts.jsonl, kb/target-facts.jsonl (including the T-t10-* rows new to this ceremony), kb/reference-facts.jsonl and kb/research.jsonl. Converted to sourced only when a verbatim quote from a cited record supported the row's own specific claim, not merely its vocabulary: 7 conversions found this way (build-evidence-record instr 'correct a record only by appending another' and invariant 'records are chained the way the hash-chained task store is' on F-a5-04/F-a5-03's append-only and chain-detection language, and best_practice on the ~2,445-records-across-308-runs figure quoted verbatim from F-a5-04; build-interface-versioning instr 'express the interface version as the profile of that standard we speak' on F-b1-03's 'adopt it whole rather than modelling our own shape', instr 'carry the version in a metadata field or header' on the REST-versioning research record's 'most-correct way of versioning your API', invariant 'every call carries an interface_version_declaration' on the MCP per-request-versioning research record, and invariant on the frozen core field set on the OTel resource-attribute research record's 'MUST NOT be ever changed'). One attempted conversion (build-interface-versioning not_exposed 'an adapter's release number ... is never surfaced as the interface version', on F-part-c-09) was reverted after render_skill/validate_skills showed it would restate F-part-c-09 under a quote agentic-stack and build-adapter-pair already hold in this skill's builds_on chain; F-part-c-09's short text has only two natural substrings and both were already claimed, so the row was left proposed with that collision named in its research query instead. No REF-anchored row and no pure references/*.md navigational pointer was converted or given an added query, matching the sourcing-01/02b/02c precedent that such rows are not researchable in the same sense (build-adapter-pair step 9, build-ceremony step 10, build-entry-conformance step 10 and its four REF-anchored rows, and build-evidence-record step 10). No row was deleted outright: the two clearest same-skill restatements found (build-ceremony's review-record and improve-record instructions, each re-enumerating the exact required-field list already defined in this skill's own contract.shapes JSON schema, one of them also re-stating the decline invariant) were trimmed to a one-clause pointer at the shape/invariant already carrying that content rather than deleted wholesale, since the surrounding step still names a distinct, non-restated action (verifying findings, or re-rendering and re-validating). The remaining 40 rows had a concrete, specific research query appended verbatim to their text or action field naming what a fetched source would need to establish to convert the row; rows that already carried a research query before this ceremony (9 across the six skills) were left as they were.
quality_note: Every candidate quote was checked as a literal substring of its row's cited kb record (via python3 tools/kb.py show <id>) before conversion, mirroring tools/validate_skills.py's walk_sourced check including its json.dumps fallback for research.jsonl records with no text field. Cross-skill quote reuse was checked against each edited skill's builds_on chain: the not_exposed reversion above is the one case a collision was actually found and undone; the four other conversions and the two build-evidence-record ones were checked and found clean. python3 tools/render_skill.py and python3 tools/validate_skills.py --only <skill> were run after every skill, each compared against its git-stash baseline before editing: final result is 0 errors for all six skills, and every pre-existing warning (10 for build-adapter-pair, 0 for build-ceremony, 1 for build-definition-of-done, 0 for build-entry-conformance, 4 for build-evidence-record, 1 for build-interface-versioning) is byte-identical in count and content to the pre-ceremony baseline - no new warning was introduced under any of the six skills' names.
